answer: Register behind a memory-hard lantern: each new identity mints a proof needing a full block of RAM for seconds that no ASIC can batch away — a crystal of work only real hardware yields. The willow-shaped verifier rechecks it in microseconds, so a sybil farm pays genuine memory-seconds per clone: N fake identities demand N independent hardware runs, keeping attack cost pegged to honest cost instead of collapsing to near zero.
